Sebuleni Pro Max AI - Master Implementation Plan

This document translates the approved SRS into a dependency-aware implementation roadmap. It divides the project into phases, independent units, integration checkpoints, milestone-safe increments, testing obligations, and a final definition of done.

Contents

  1. Planning principles
  2. Implementation units
  3. Dependency graph
  4. Integration strategy
  5. Phase-by-phase development plan
  6. Milestones
  7. Testing strategy by phase
  8. Definition of done
  9. Final project completion checklist

Planning principles

  • Every unit has one primary responsibility.
  • Units integrate in dependency order and produce working increments.
  • No phase leaves the system in a broken state.
  • Data leakage prevention, deterministic preprocessing, and reproducibility are first-class design constraints.
  • CLI, API, and batch reporting are integrated only after deterministic data and model contracts are stable.
  • Auto-promotion is out of scope for v1; retraining flows must remain review-gated.

U1 Configuration and contracts

ObjectiveDefine all configuration schemas, data contracts, and validation models for deterministic operation.
ScopeYAML schema loading, typed config objects, environment overrides, request/response contracts, and shared validation logic.
Files to create or modifytraining/config_loader.py, training/config_schema.py, api/schemas.py, training/contracts.py, config/base.yaml, config/instrument.example.yaml
Public interfacesload_config(), validate_config(), typed config classes, API request/response models.
InputsYAML files, environment variables, API payloads, CLI arguments.
OutputsValidated immutable runtime configuration and shared contracts.

U2 OHLC ingestion, calendar normalization, and resampling

FieldDefinition
ObjectiveCreate a deterministic ingestion and resampling pipeline for the active multi-timeframe stack built from 1-minute OHLC input.
ScopeInput validation, timezone normalization, session handling, weekend and holiday rules, DST-safe daily close handling, and OHLC aggregation from 1m into 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d.
Files to create or modifytraining/data_loader.py, training/calendar.py, training/resample.py, training/data_quality.py
Public interfacesload_ohlc_frame(), normalize_calendar(), resample_timeframes(), validate_bar_sequence()
InputsValidated config, raw OHLC file(s).
OutputsValidated 1-minute bars and derived 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, and 1d bars, all aligned for multi-timeframe modeling.
DependenciesU1.
Internal componentsTimezone mapper, session boundary resolver, weekend and holiday filters, resample engine, quality checks.
Acceptance criteriaNo timestamp misalignment, no silent corrections, deterministic identical output for identical input.
Unit testing requirementsTimezone, DST, duplicate timestamp, missing bar, daily close, OHLC aggregation tests.
Integration testing requirementsInstrument config plus OHLC file produces fully aligned multi-timeframe output.
Potential risksTimezone bugs, session drift, ambiguous holiday handling.

U3 Deterministic feature engineering

FieldDefinition
ObjectiveGenerate reproducible OHLC-derived and calendar-derived features for each modeled timeframe.
ScopeReturns, ranges, wick and body ratios, rolling statistics, session flags, and multi-timeframe alignment-ready feature windows.
Files to create or modifytraining/features.py, training/windowing.py, training/feature_registry.py
Public interfacesbuild_features(), build_windows(), list_enabled_features()
InputsResampled OHLC frames from U2, config feature toggles.
OutputsAligned feature matrices and window tensors keyed by timeframe and reference timestamp.
DependenciesU1, U2.

Acceptance criteriaAll feature generation is causal, deterministic, and explainable.
Unit testing requirementsDeterminism tests, leakage tests, feature correctness tests for small bar sequences.
Integration testing requirementsResampled data plus config produces expected window shapes for all timeframes.
Potential risksHidden future leakage through rolling calculations.

Files to create or modifytraining/splits.py, training/folds.py, training/eval_contract.py

Integration strategy

Integration order

  1. Stabilize config and contracts before any data pipeline implementation.
  2. Integrate ingestion, calendar logic, resampling, and features as one deterministic offline chain.
  3. Add labeling and walk-forward folds before any model code.
  4. Integrate backbone and heads into the training runner before explanation or serving work.
  5. Add explanation retrieval only after stable latent outputs exist.
  6. Add inference runtime after a walk-forward model can be trained and loaded.
  7. Add API, CLI, and reports after inference contracts are stable.
  8. Add monitoring and controlled retraining last, because they depend on all operational contracts.

Required interfaces and contracts

  • U1 defines shared typed contracts that all later units must consume unchanged unless the SRS is amended.
  • U2 and U3 must expose deterministic data and feature contracts identical between training and inference.
  • U4 and U5 define label and fold semantics that training and evaluation must not reinterpret.
  • U6 and U7 expose stable tensor and prediction interfaces consumed by U8, U9, and U10.
  • U10 owns the canonical prediction payload contract for U11 and U12.

Backward compatibility considerations

  • Prediction response schema must remain backward compatible once API clients are introduced.
  • Config keys must be versioned if renamed or retired.
  • Model artifacts must retain metadata needed for replay and audit after retraining.

Regression risks

  • Changes to resampling or session logic can invalidate labels, folds, and trained models simultaneously.
  • Changes to runtime feature logic can break training-inference parity.
  • Changes to explanation templates can introduce nondeterminism or contradiction without affecting core prediction metrics.

Phase-by-phase development plan

Phase Units Primary outcome
Phase 1 - Contracts and deterministic data foundation U1, U2, U3 Validated OHLC ingestion, session-safe resampling, and deterministic feature windows.
Phase 2 - Labeling and evaluation foundation U4, U5 Approved target semantics and leak-free walk-forward folds.
Phase 3 - Core predictive model U6, U7 Trainable multi-timeframe model with all prediction heads.
Phase 4 - Explanation and evaluation runner U8, U9 Grounded explanations plus reproducible training and evaluation workflows.
Phase 5 - Operator surfaces U10, U11 Production-facing inference, API, CLI, and report generation.
Phase 6 - Operations and controlled retraining U12 Monitoring, scheduled jobs, and review-gated retraining lifecycle.

Milestones

Milestone 1 - Deterministic preprocessing baseline

Delivers validated config, OHLC ingestion, calendar normalization, deterministic resampling, and feature generation. The system is not predictive yet, but it can load data, produce aligned windows, and fail correctly on malformed input.

Milestone 2 - Target and validation baseline

Delivers event labeling, boundary and timing labels, ambiguity handling, and walk-forward fold generation. At this point the project has a reliable offline research foundation with no model training yet.

Milestone 3 - Trainable predictive core

Delivers backbone, heads, and training orchestration. The system can complete a full walk-forward training and output predictive metrics.

Milestone 4 - Explainable offline candidate

Adds analog retrieval and deterministic explanation generation. The system can now produce prediction plus evidence on offline evaluation data.

Milestone 5 - Live operator-ready inference

Delivers loaded-model inference, REST API, CLI, and batch reporting. The operator can serve predictions and generate reports from one machine.

Milestone 6 - Operationally governed v1

Delivers monitoring, scheduled reporting, retraining request flows, review-gated candidate handling, and rollback-safe governance.

Testing strategy by phase

Phase Unit tests Integration tests Regression focus
Phase 1 Config, schema, timezone, DST, resampling, feature determinism Raw OHLC to aligned multi-timeframe feature windows Timestamp correctness, no silent drops
Phase 2 Threshold-cross semantics, maturity detection, fold generation Features plus labels plus walk-forward partitions No label leakage, no fold overlap
Phase 3 Model shape, loss, device, determinism, calibration hooks One fold training plus evaluation pipeline Training stability, task-output consistency
Phase 4 Retrieval determinism, explanation grounding, contradiction guards Offline predictions plus analog evidence generation No future contamination in retrieval index
Phase 5 API validation, CLI parsing, report serialization Train, load, predict, and generate reports end to end Prediction payload compatibility, latency bounds
Phase 6 Threshold alerts, schedule policies, approval guards Scheduled review, retraining request, candidate approval or rejection No unsafe promotion, no broken review chain

Definition of done

An implementation unit is complete only when all of the following are true:

  1. Implementation is complete.
  2. Static analysis passes.
  3. Type checking passes.
  4. Unit tests pass.
  5. Integration tests pass.
  6. Documentation is updated.
  7. Public APIs are documented.
  8. Code review is complete.
Completion rule

No unit may be marked complete if its interface contract is undocumented, if it introduces nondeterministic preprocessing without explicit approval, or if it leaves a downstream unit unable to integrate cleanly.

Final project completion checklist

  1. SRS approved.
  2. Implementation plan approved.
  3. All units implemented in dependency order.
  4. All public contracts documented and versioned.
  5. Data leakage tests passing.
  6. Determinism checks passing under fixed seed.
  7. CPU and CUDA execution paths verified where supported.
  8. Walk-forward evaluation completed and archived.
  9. Acceptance thresholds met or explicitly waived with written approval.
  10. Inference latency verified on target machine.
  11. Explanation reliability tests passing.
  12. CLI, API, and batch reporting workflows tested end to end.
  13. Monitoring and retraining review workflows tested end to end.
  14. Documentation updated for setup, operation, retraining review, and failure handling.
  15. Final code review completed.
This roadmap is intended to be executed only after explicit approval of the SRS and this plan.
